text:
mila (product): Quick sync — predictive-burst routing feature: aiming for pilot next week. Need final decisions on SLA wording, pricing knob, runbook, and docs. Who can own what?

josh (eng): I can own the SLA latency/availability metrics. Question — do we want a strict 99.9% p99 response latency target for pilot or a softer internal SLO?

mila (product): For pilot let's make it an internal SLO (p99 < 450ms) and only promise an availability SLO (99.9%) externally. That keeps legal/ops exposure low.

sara (docs): I'll draft a short "what to expect" page and an FAQ. Need the exact SLO strings to put in the customer-facing doc. Also a snippet for pricing examples.

josh (eng): Noted. I'll post p99 numbers from the staging run by EOD. Also: routing can degrade to fallback model under load — we should document that as graceful degradation.

deepak (sre): Runbook + oncall: I can author the runbook if you give me the failure modes list (RPC timeouts, queue saturation, KV cache thrashing). Ops-bot: create ticket?#failure-mode\.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-predictive-burst-failmodes (assigned to deepak).

lina (support): Support playbook: escalate to eng after 15m if >10 customers affected or error rate >5% for 5m. Also need canned responses for customers about billing impact.

mila (product): Good escalation thresholds. For billing: we need a toggle for burst pricing that is opt-in per-customer. Pricing team prefers usage-based with a burst multiplier; let's aim for 1.5x during bursts and show a dashboard metric.

sara (docs): Confirming: I'll include a sample invoice line: "Burst routing surcharge (opt-in) — 1.5x tokens during burst windows" and an example table. Want wording review from finance before publishing.

josh (eng): Implementation note: config flag `routing.burst_opt_in` and `burst_multiplier: 1.5`. We'll default to off. Sample config:```yaml
routing:
  burst_opt_in: false
  burst_multiplier: 1.5
``` 

deepak (sre): Runbook skeleton I propose: detection -> attempt auto-throttle -> switch to fallback model -> notify oncall -> rollback routing policy. I'll push a PR to the runbooks repo.

lina (support): Also include a customer communication template: short, no-blame, with expected timeline and workaround (disable opt-in). I can draft.

mila (product): Owners: SLA & metrics -> @josh; runbook -> @deepak; customer docs + FAQ + pricing example -> @sara + finance review; support templates -> @lina. Next check-in tomorrow 10:30 PT. Any blockers?

josh (eng): Blocker: need clarity on whether fallback model must be same-size instance or lower-capacity quantized variant. Prefer automated fallback to a cheaper variant to preserve capacity.

mila (product): OK allow fallback to quantized variant for pilot but annotate possible quality differences in the FAQ.

sara (docs): I'll add a short paragraph: "Fallback behavior — reduced model variant may be used to maintain availability; slight changes in output may occur."

deepak (sre): I'll add SLO alert thresholds: p99 latency > 600ms for 5m -> pager, error rate > 3% for 5m -> pager. Non-pager runbook steps for lower severity.

lina (support): Adding to the support doc: how to check routing state in Console and billing preview. Will sync with docs once draft is up.

mila (product): Great. Action items recap: josh posts staging p99 numbers + confirm fallback variant; deepak pushes runbook PR; sara drafts customer page + get finance signoff on wording; lina drafts support templates. Tomorrow 10:30 PT we finalize public wording and toggle schedule. :thumbsup:

josh (eng): Will post numbers by 18:00 PT today.

sara (docs): I'll share a draft link in #product-docs when ready.

(ended thread)
